questions.question: ____ concluded that not only does the earth attract an apple and the moon, but all objects in the universe attract each other.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Isaac Newton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sir **Isaac Newton** formulated the **Universal Law of Gravitation** in **1687**, which he documented in his landmark publication **Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica**.
 
• Newton observed that the same force responsible for an **apple falling** to the ground also keeps the **Moon** in its nearly circular orbit around the **Earth**.
 
• He concluded that **gravitation** is a universal phenomenon; every point mass attracts every other point mass in the universe by a force pointing along the line intersecting both points.
 
• This law states that the force is proportional to the **product of their masses** (m1 × m2) and inversely proportional to the **square of the distance** (r²) between them.
 
• His work unified **terrestrial** and **celestial mechanics**, proving that the laws of physics are consistent throughout the entire universe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Albert Einstein**:

 
 
• Introduced the **General Theory of Relativity** in **1915**, explaining gravity as the warping of **spacetime** rather than a simple pulling force.
 
• Developed the mass-energy equivalence formula **E = mc²**, which is a cornerstone of modern physics.
 
 
 
• **Galileo Galilei**:
 
 
• Often called the **Father of Modern Science**, he pioneered the use of the **telescope** for astronomical discovery.
 
• He studied the **uniform acceleration** of falling objects and challenged the Aristotelian view that heavier objects fall faster.
 
 
 
• **Thomas Edison**:
 
 
• A prolific inventor who held **1,093 US patents**, focusing on **electrical power generation**, **mass communication**, and **sound recording**.
 
• Key inventions include the **phonograph** and the first commercially practical **incandescent light bulb**.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Constant (G)**:
 
 
• The numerical value of **G** (approximately 6.674 × 10−¹¹ Nm²/kg²) was accurately measured for the first time by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798**.

questions.question: Which of the following is an ore of mercury?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cinnabar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cinnabar** is the primary and most common ore of **mercury (Hg)**.
 
• Chemically, it is known as **Mercury(II) sulfide** and its chemical formula is **HgS**.
 
• It typically appears as a **bright red** or **brownish-red** crystalline solid, which has been historically used as a **pigment** known as **vermilion**.
 
• The extraction of mercury from cinnabar involves **roasting** the ore in a furnace. During this process, **sulfur** in the ore combines with **oxygen** to form sulfur dioxide, and the mercury **vaporizes**.
 
• The mercury vapor is then **cooled** and **condensed** to collect **liquid mercury**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bauxite**:

 
 
• It is the principal ore of **Aluminium (Al)**.
 
• It is not a specific mineral but a **sedimentary rock** with high aluminum content, primarily consisting of **gibbsite**, **boehmite**, and **diaspore**.
 
• **Australia** is the world's largest producer of bauxite, while in **India**, the state of **Odisha** is the leading producer.
 
 
 
• **Magnetite**:
 
 
• It is one of the most important ores of **Iron (Fe)**.
 
• Its chemical formula is **Fe3O4** and it is known for its **natural magnetic** properties, often called **lodestone**.
 
• It has a very high iron content, approximately **72.4%**, making it a high-quality ore.
 
 
 
• **Malachite**:
 
 
• It is a **copper carbonate hydroxide** mineral with the formula **Cu2CO3(OH)2**.
 
• It is a minor ore of **Copper (Cu)** and is easily recognizable by its distinct **bright green** color.
 
• It was often used as a **mineral pigment** in green paints in ancient times.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mercury (Hg)**: It is also known as **quicksilver** and is the only common metal that is **liquid** at standard temperature and pressure.
 
• **Applications**: Due to its uniform **thermal expansion**, mercury is used in **thermometers**, **barometers**, and **manometers**. It is also used in **fluorescent lighting** and **dental amalgams**.
 
• **Amalgams**: Mercury can dissolve many other metals (like gold and silver) to form alloys called **amalgams**. However, it does not form amalgams with **iron**, which is why it is often stored in **iron flasks**.
 
• **Toxicity**: Mercury is highly **toxic** to humans. **Minamata disease** is a neurological syndrome caused by severe **mercury poisoning**, famously occurring in **Japan** in the **1950s**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately reflects the biomechanical coordination during the throwing phase of discus throw?

options.text: The shoulders and trunk continue rotating till 1 minute after the discus is released to maintain momentum.
The left foot remains fixed while the right foot rotates and stays straight throughout the motion.
Both knees stay straight during rotation, but the right knee bends after forward extension for balance.
The body's weight shifts entirely to the left foot while the right leg stabilizes the upper body lean.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The biomechanical coordination during the throwing phase in discus throw involves the bending of the **right knee** after forward extension for balance, which stabilizes the body and enhances the accuracy of the throw. Hence, statement 3 is correct. 
• The shoulders and trunk do not continue rotating for 1 minute after the discus is released. The rotation stops immediately after the release to prevent unnecessary loss of energy. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect. 
• The left foot does not remain fixed during the throwing phase. Both feet contribute to rotational force, and the movement of the feet is crucial for generating momentum. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect. 
• The body’s weight does not shift entirely to the left foot while the right leg stabilizes the upper body lean. The weight distribution varies throughout the phases, ensuring proper momentum and balance during the throw. Hence, statement 4 is incorrect. 
• The correct biomechanical technique involves bending the **right knee** after forward extension to maintain balance and maximize the throw’s efficiency. This technique is crucial for proper stabilization. Hence, statement 3 is correct. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Biomechanics in Discus Throw:** 
• The discus throw involves coordinated movements of the **lower limbs, trunk, and upper limbs** to generate rotational force and release the discus at an optimal angle. 
• The **right knee** bending after forward extension is crucial for maintaining balance and stabilizing the body during the critical release phase. 
• The shoulders and trunk rotation play a significant role in generating angular momentum, but the rotation stops immediately after the throw. 
• **Phases of Discus Throw:** 
• It includes the **wind-up phase**, where the thrower builds initial momentum by rotating the trunk and arms. 
• The **transition phase** involves shifting the weight between the feet to prepare for rotational acceleration. 
• The **delivery phase** is where the discus is released, requiring precise coordination and balance. 
• The **follow-through phase** ensures that the thrower maintains balance and avoids injury. 
• **Key Techniques in Discus Throw:** 
• The thrower should focus on maintaining a **low center of gravity** for stability during rotational movements. 
• The discus is released at an optimal angle, typically between **35-45 degrees**, for maximum distance. 
• Proper foot placement and rotation are essential for generating torque and transferring energy to the discus. 
• **Applications in Sports Science:** 
• Understanding biomechanics in discus throw helps athletes improve their performance and minimize the risk of injuries. 
• It allows coaches to analyze movements and suggest corrective measures for better technique. 
• Sports scientists use motion capture technology to study the kinematics and dynamics of the throw. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Context:** 
• The discus throw has its origins in ancient Greece and was part of the **Olympic Games** as early as 708 BC. 
• Modern techniques were developed in the **19th century**, with emphasis on rotational movements. 
• **Physics in Discus Throw:** 
• The throw involves concepts such as **angular momentum, torque, and projectile motion**. 
• The distance covered by the discus depends on the release velocity, angle, and height. 
• **Training Essentials:** 
• Athletes undergo **strength training** to develop core stability and rotational power. 
• They practice drills to enhance footwork and improve timing during the throw.

questions.question: What specific physical quantity ensures a satellite maintains its orbit without continuous propulsion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Orbital velocity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Orbital velocity** is the speed required for a satellite to maintain its orbit around a celestial body, like Earth, without propulsion or falling back due to gravity.
 
• It is determined by the balance between the satellite's inertia (from its motion) and the gravitational pull of the planet it is orbiting. This ensures the satellite remains in a stable orbit.
 
• For a satellite to remain in orbit, its **orbital velocity** must match the gravitational force pulling it toward the planet. If the velocity is too high, the satellite will escape into space; if too low, it will fall back to Earth.
 
• The formula for orbital velocity is given by **v = √(GM/r)**, where **G** is the gravitational constant, **M** is the mass of the celestial body, and **r** is the radius of the orbit.
 
• **Atmospheric drag** can influence orbital velocity in low Earth orbits, causing satellites to lose speed and eventually deorbit. However, in the absence of atmospheric drag in higher orbits, orbital velocity alone ensures stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mass:** A satellite's mass does not directly determine its orbit. While mass affects gravitational attraction, the satellite's orbital velocity is independent of its weight.
 
• **Gravitational pull:** The gravitational pull of a planet provides the force that keeps the satellite in orbit. However, it needs to be balanced by the satellite's orbital velocity to ensure stable motion.
 
• **Atmospheric drag:** This factor is significant in low Earth orbits (LEO). Atmospheric particles can slow the satellite over time, causing it to lose altitude and eventually re-enter the atmosphere.
 
• **Examples:** Geostationary satellites, such as communication satellites, maintain their orbit by traveling at speeds matching the Earth's rotation, ensuring they appear stationary from the surface.
 
• **Applications of Orbital Velocity:** Orbital velocity is crucial for launching satellites, space exploration, and maintaining space stations like the International Space Station (ISS). It ensures that objects remain in their designated trajectories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO):** Satellites in LEO typically have orbital velocities of around **7.8 km/s**. They are closer to Earth, making them more prone to atmospheric drag.
 
• **Geostationary Orbit:** Satellites in geostationary orbit (~36,000 km above Earth) travel at a speed of approximately **3.07 km/s**. This ensures they remain fixed relative to Earth's surface.
 
• **Escape Velocity:** If a satellite's speed exceeds the escape velocity (~11.2 km/s for Earth), it will leave Earth's gravitational influence and move into interplanetary space.
 
• **Space Missions:** Missions like **ISRO's Chandrayaan** and NASA's Mars rovers calculate orbital and escape velocities accurately for successful launches and operations.
 
• **Newton's Laws:** Orbital velocity is derived using **Newton's Laws of Motion** and Universal Gravitation. These principles explain the relationship between force, mass, and motion in orbit.

questions.question: The first peptide to be produced after wounding in the tomato plant is ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Systemin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Systemin** is an **18-amino acid peptide** that acts as a primary signaling molecule in **tomato plants** (**Solanum lycopersicum**) and other members of the **Solanaceae** family. It was the **first peptide hormone** ever discovered in plants, identified in **1991** by the research team led by **Clarence A. Ryan**.
 
• The peptide is released from a much larger precursor protein called **prosystemin**, which contains **200 amino acids**. Upon **wounding** caused by **herbivorous insects** or mechanical damage, prosystemin is proteolytically processed to release the active **systemin**.
 
• Its primary function is to mediate the **systemic wound response**. Once released at the site of injury, it travels through the **phloem** to distant leaves, acting as a long-distance signal to prepare the entire plant for potential further attack.
 
• In the target cells, **Systemin** binds to a **cell surface receptor** (**SR160**, a member of the **Leucine-Rich Repeat Receptor-Like Kinase** family). This binding triggers a signaling cascade that activates the **octadecanoid pathway**, eventually leading to the synthesis of **Jasmonic Acid**.
 
• The ultimate result of this signaling is the **induction of defense genes**, most notably those encoding **Protease Inhibitors (PIs)**. These inhibitors interfere with the **digestive enzymes** of insects, making the plant tissues indigestible and deterring further feeding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jasmonic Acid (JA):**

 
 
• **Jasmonic acid** is a **lipid-derived hormone** synthesized from **linolenic acid** via the **octadecanoid pathway**. While it is crucial for wounding defense, it is a **small molecule hormone**, not a peptide. It works downstream of **Systemin** to activate the **transcription** of defense proteins.
 
 
 
• **Salicylic Acid (SA):**
 
 
• **Salicylic acid** is a **phenolic phytohormone** primarily involved in **Systemic Acquired Resistance (SAR)**. It plays a major role in defending the plant against **biotrophic pathogens** (which feed on living tissue). Unlike systemin, which responds to **chewing insects**, SA is the lead signal for **microbial infections**.
 
 
 
• **Ricin:**
 
 
• **Ricin** is a highly potent **toxin** found in the **seeds** of the **Castor oil plant** (**Ricinus communis**). It is a **Type II ribosome-inactivating protein (RIP)** that inhibits **protein synthesis** in eukaryotic cells. It is **not a signaling peptide** involved in tomato plant wounding but is a chemical defense against ingestion.
 
 
 
• **Ethylene:**
 
 
• **Ethylene** is a **gaseous plant hormone** that often works in synergy with **Jasmonic acid** during the wound response. It is involved in **fruit ripening**, **senescence**, and **abscission**, as well as reacting to **necrotrophic pathogens**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **discovery of Systemin** challenged the long-held belief that plant hormones were only **small molecules** like **auxins**, **gibberellins**, and **cytokinins**. It established that **peptides** could also serve as potent **long-distance messengers** in plants.
 
• **Phloem transport:** The ability of **Systemin** to move through the **sieve tubes** of the **phloem** allows the plant to coordinate a **whole-body defense** within **hours** of an localized attack.
 
• **Specificity:** While **Systemin** is specific to **Solanaceous** plants, other plant families use different **Peptide Elucidators (Peps)** to achieve similar **immune responses**.

questions.question: What is another use of bleaching powder besides bleaching?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Disinfecting drinking water**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bleaching powder**, chemically known as **Calcium Oxychloride** (CaOCl₂), is extensively used as a **disinfectant** for drinking water to make it free from **germs** and **pathogens**.
 
• When bleaching powder is added to water, it releases **chlorine**, which acts as a powerful **germicide** that kills bacteria and other microorganisms, ensuring the water is safe for consumption.
 
• **Making soap** and **making detergent** primarily involve the process of **saponification**, which uses fats or oils and strong alkalis like **Sodium Hydroxide** (NaOH) or **Potassium Hydroxide** (KOH), rather than bleaching powder.
 
• **Making paint** involves pigments, binders, and solvents; bleaching powder is not a standard ingredient in the manufacturing of paint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bleaching powder is produced by the action of **chlorine gas** on **dry slaked lime** [Ca(OH)₂].
 
• It is used as a strong **oxidizing agent** in many chemical industries due to its ability to release oxygen.
 
• In the **textile industry**, it is used for bleaching **cotton** and **linen**, and in the **paper industry**, it is used for bleaching **wood pulp**.
 
• It is also used for **bleaching washed clothes** in laundries and for the **unshrinkable** treatment of wool.
 
• Bleaching powder should be stored in a cool, dry place because it loses its **chlorine content** when exposed to air or moisture.

questions.question: Which mission by ISRO aims to explore Venus and study its atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shukrayaan-1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shukrayaan-1** is the planned mission by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to study the planet **Venus** and its atmosphere.
 
• The name is derived from the Sanskrit words **'Shukra'**, which means Venus, and **'Yaan'**, which means craft or vehicle.
 
• The mission aims to explore the **surface geology**, **stratigraphy**, and the **atmospheric composition** of Venus, which is known for its extremely dense and hot atmosphere.
 
• **Mangalyaan-2** (Mars Orbiter Mission 2) is a follow-up mission to **Mars** to further study the Red Planet.
 
• **Gaganyaan** is India's first **Human Spaceflight Programme**, intended to send Indian astronauts (Gaganaut) into a **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.
 
• **Chandrayaan-4** is a proposed **Lunar Sample Return Mission** aimed at bringing back soil and rock samples from the **Moon** to Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Venus is often called **'Earth's Twin'** because of its similar size and mass, but it has a runaway **greenhouse effect** that makes it the hottest planet in our solar system.
 
• The **Union Cabinet** of India recently approved the **Venus Orbiter Mission (VOM)**, with a targeted launch window around **March 2028**.
 
• The mission is expected to use a **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)** to peer through the thick clouds of Venus and map its surface.
 
• **ISRO** was founded on **August 15, 1969**, and its current headquarters are located in **Bengaluru**, Karnataka.
 
• The successful execution of this mission will make India one of the few nations to have sent a probe to Venus, following the **Soviet Union**, **USA**, **European Space Agency**, and **Japan**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to dimensional analysis?

options.text: An equation that is dimensionally consistent is always physically correct.
Dimensional analysis can verify both the magnitude and the physical validity of an equation.
Trigonometric and logarithmic functions are valid only when applied to quantities that are dimensionless.
Refractive index has dimensions because it involves the speed of light.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Trigonometric and logarithmic functions are valid only when applied to quantities that are dimensionless.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential functions** are mathematical operations that must take **dimensionless arguments**. For example, in the expression sin(theta) , the angle theta must be dimensionless. Similarly, in log(x) or e^x , x must be a pure number.
 
• An equation that is **dimensionally consistent** is not necessarily **physically correct**. For instance, the equation s = ut + at² is dimensionally consistent (all terms have dimensions of length), but it is physically incorrect because the correct kinematic formula is s = ut + (1)/(2)at² .
 
• **Dimensional analysis** cannot verify the **magnitude** or **dimensionless constants** in an equation. It only checks if the units on both sides of the equation are compatible.
 
• The **Refractive Index** is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in a medium ( n = c/v ). Since it is a ratio of two similar physical quantities (speeds), it is a **dimensionless quantity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Principle of Homogeneity of Dimensions** states that the dimensions of all the terms in a physical expression must be the same.
 
• Other common **dimensionless quantities** include **strain**, **relative density**, **solid angle**, and **plane angle**.
 
• While dimensional analysis is a powerful tool for checking the consistency of equations and deriving relations, its main limitation is its inability to determine **proportionality constants** or handle **summation/difference** of terms that are not of the same dimension.

questions.question: What is the name of the layer of the Earth's atmosphere where weather phenomena occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Troposphere**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Troposphere** is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere and is the region where we live. It contains approximately **75% to 80%** of the total mass of the atmosphere.
 
• Almost all **weather phenomena**, including cloud formation, rain, snow, and storms, occur in this layer because it contains nearly all of the atmosphere's **water vapor** and **aerosols**.
 
• In the troposphere, the temperature generally **decreases with altitude** at a rate known as the environmental lapse rate.
 
• The **Stratosphere** is the layer above the troposphere; it contains the **Ozone Layer** and is relatively stable, which is why commercial jet aircraft often fly in its lower parts to avoid weather disturbances.
 
• The **Mesosphere** is the third layer where temperatures drop to their lowest in the atmosphere and where most **meteors** burn up upon entry.
 
• The **Thermosphere** is a high-altitude layer where temperatures increase significantly with height and contains the **Ionosphere**, which is crucial for **radio communication**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The boundary that separates the troposphere from the stratosphere is called the **Tropopause**.
 
• The height of the troposphere varies with latitude; it is thickest at the **Equator** (about 18 km) and thinnest at the **Poles** (about 8 km) due to the differences in solar heating and centrifugal force.
 
• The **Exosphere** is the outermost layer of the Earth's atmosphere, extending into space, where the air is extremely thin.
 
• The atmosphere is composed mainly of **Nitrogen** (78%) and **Oxygen** (21%), with trace amounts of other gases like Argon and Carbon Dioxide.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of meristematic tissues in plants?

options.text: Large vacuoles and thick cell walls
Absence of nucleus and presence of lignified walls
Actively dividing cells with dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei
Dead cells that provide mechanical support

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Actively dividing cells with dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Meristematic tissues** consist of actively dividing cells that are responsible for plant growth.
 
• Cells in meristematic tissues have a **dense cytoplasm** and lack large vacuoles, which allows efficient division.
 
• These cells possess **prominent nuclei** to control cell division and metabolic activities.
 
• The cell walls in meristematic tissues are **thin and non-lignified**, facilitating flexibility during cell division.
 
• Meristematic tissues are located in specific regions such as **apical meristems, lateral meristems, and intercalary meristems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apical Meristems**: Found at the tips of roots and shoots, responsible for primary growth (increase in length).
 
• **Lateral Meristems**: Located in the sides of stems and roots, responsible for secondary growth (increase in thickness).
 
• **Intercalary Meristems**: Present at the base of leaves or internodes, aiding in regrowth of grass and other monocots.
 
• Meristematic cells lack **large vacuoles** because vacuoles are primarily used for storage, which is not needed during active division.
 
• Meristematic cells eventually differentiate into permanent tissues, which perform specific functions such as support, transport, or photosynthesis.

questions.question: Deoxygenated blood from the body enters through which of the following chamber of the heart of humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right atrium**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• Deoxygenated blood from various parts of the body returns to the heart through two large veins - the **superior vena cava** and the **inferior vena cava**. 
• The superior vena cava collects blood from the upper part of the body (head, neck, arms), while the inferior vena cava collects blood from the lower part of the body (abdomen, legs). 
• Both these veins empty deoxygenated blood into the **right atrium**, which is the first chamber of the heart to receive this blood. 
• From the right atrium, the blood is pushed into the **right ventricle** during atrial contraction. 
• The right atrium plays a crucial role in the circulation of blood as it acts as a receiving chamber for deoxygenated blood, initiating the pulmonary circulation process to re-oxygenate the blood. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Heart Chambers and Their Functions:** 
• The human heart has **four chambers**: the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle. 
• The **right atrium** receives deoxygenated blood from the body and pumps it into the right ventricle. 
• The **right ventricle** pumps the blood to the lungs for oxygenation through the pulmonary artery. 
• The **left atrium** receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and sends it to the left ventricle. 
• The **left ventricle** pumps the oxygenated blood to the entire body through the aorta. 
• **Pulmonary Circulation:** 
• Deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle to the lungs through the **pulmonary artery**. 
• In the lungs, carbon dioxide is exchanged for oxygen in the alveoli (tiny air sacs). 
• The oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium of the heart via the **pulmonary veins**. 
• **Systemic Circulation:** 
• Oxygenated blood is pumped from the left ventricle to the entire body through the **aorta**. 
• The body tissues utilize oxygen and nutrients from the blood, and in return, the blood picks up carbon dioxide and waste products. 
• Deoxygenated blood is then returned to the right atrium through the superior and inferior vena cavae. 
• **Valves of the Heart:** 
• The heart has four major valves to ensure the unidirectional flow of blood: **tricuspid valve, pulmonary valve, mitral valve, and aortic valve**. 
• The **tricuspid valve** is located between the right atrium and right ventricle, preventing backflow of blood. 
• The **pulmonary valve** lies between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery, regulating blood flow to the lungs. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The **right atrium** is part of the systemic circulation and acts as the entry point for blood returning from the body. 
• The separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood in the heart's chambers is critical for efficient circulation in humans and other mammals. 
• The heart beats approximately **72 times per minute** on average, ensuring continuous circulation of blood. 
• Any obstruction in the flow of blood to or from the right atrium can lead to serious cardiovascular conditions, such as **right heart failure**. </ul

questions.question: Which energy source cannot be replenished naturally in a short period of time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Natural Gas**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Natural Gas** is classified as a **non-renewable energy source** because it takes millions of years to form from the remains of ancient marine organisms buried under layers of sediment and subjected to intense heat and pressure.
 
• Because the formation process of **fossil fuels** occurs over **geological timescales**, they cannot be replenished naturally in a short period of time once they are consumed.
 
• **Wind**, **Solar**, and **Hydroelectric** energy are **renewable resources**. These sources are constantly replenished by natural processes such as the **water cycle**, **solar radiation**, and **atmospheric circulation**.
 
• **Renewable energy** is considered sustainable because it is virtually inexhaustible on a human timeframe, unlike **finite resources** like natural gas, coal, and oil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fossil fuels** (coal, petroleum, and natural gas) currently supply a large portion of the world's energy but are the primary drivers of **climate change** due to the emission of **carbon dioxide (CO2)** and other **greenhouse gases**.
 
• **Natural gas** is primarily composed of **methane (CH4)**. While it burns cleaner than coal, it is still a significant source of carbon emissions.
 
• The global shift toward **green energy** aims to replace non-renewable sources with **clean energy** alternatives like **geothermal**, **biomass**, and **tidal energy** to ensure **environmental sustainability**.
 
• **Energy conservation** and the use of **energy-efficient** technologies are also vital in reducing the rapid depletion of non-renewable resources.

questions.question: For a rigid body, the angular velocity of any particle about a given axis of rotation is:

options.text: Proportional to its distance from the axis
Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The same for all particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **rigid body**, all particles are fixed relative to each other and move collectively during rotation.
 
• The angular velocity is a measure of the rate of rotation of a body about a given axis and is denoted as **ω (omega)**.
 
• For a rigid body, the angular velocity of all particles is **the same** because they rotate together about the same axis at the same rate.
 
• While the linear velocity of particles depends on their distance from the axis of rotation, the angular velocity remains **constant** for all particles of the rigid body.
 
• This uniformity of angular velocity ensures that the body remains rigid and its shape does not change during rotation.
 
• Angular velocity is a **vector quantity**, having both magnitude and direction, where the direction is determined by the right-hand rule.
 
• The concept of angular velocity is widely used in **mechanics, engineering, and physics** to study rotational motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Proportional to its distance from the axis**__

 __
 
• The linear velocity of a particle in a rigid body is **proportional to its distance** from the axis of rotation. However, angular velocity is the same for all particles.
 
• This is because linear velocity (v) is calculated as v = ω × r, where **r** is the distance from the axis, and ω is the angular velocity.
 
 
 
• **Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because angular velocity does not depend on the distance from the axis. However, other properties, like torque, can depend inversely on certain factors.
 
 
 
• **Always zero**__
 
 
• For a rigid body in rotational motion, angular velocity is never zero unless the body is at rest.
 
• If angular velocity were zero, the body would not exhibit any rotational motion.

questions.question: Which of these biomolecules is an essential component of the plasma membrane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phospholipids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Phospholipids** are a major component of the plasma membrane, forming a bilayer that provides structure and acts as a selective barrier for the cell.
 
• Each phospholipid molecule has a hydrophilic (water-attracting) "head" and two hydrophobic (water-repelling) "tails," which arrange themselves into a bilayer to create the plasma membrane.
 
• The phospholipid bilayer is responsible for the fluidity of the membrane, allowing for the movement of proteins and lipids within it.
 
• It plays a critical role in maintaining cell integrity, enabling the transport of substances in and out of the cell, and facilitating cell signaling.
 
• Phospholipids also contribute to membrane flexibility, which is essential for processes like endocytosis, exocytosis, and cell division.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cellulose**

 
 
• Cellulose is a complex carbohydrate (polysaccharide) composed of glucose units linked by beta-1,4-glycosidic bonds.
 
• It is the primary structural component of plant cell walls, providing rigidity and support to plants.
 
• Cellulose is not present in the plasma membrane of animal cells; it is exclusive to plants and some algae.
 
 
 
• **DNA**
 
 
• DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the hereditary material in humans and most other organisms, carrying genetic instructions for development, functioning, growth, and reproduction.
 
• DNA is located within the nucleus of eukaryotic cells and is not part of the plasma membrane structure.
 
• It plays no direct role in forming or maintaining the plasma membrane but is crucial for coding the proteins that may integrate into the membrane.
 
 
 
• **Glycogen**
 
 
• Glycogen is a polysaccharide that serves as a form of energy storage in animals, fungi, and bacteria.
 
• It is stored primarily in the liver and muscle tissues and is broken down into glucose when energy is needed.
 
• Glycogen is not a structural component of the plasma membrane and serves a different biological function related to energy storage and metabolism.

questions.question: Mechanical energy is mainly composed of how many types?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mechanical energy** is primarily classified into **two types: kinetic energy and potential energy.**
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy an object possesses due to its motion. For example, a moving car or a flowing river has kinetic energy.
 
• **Potential energy** is the energy an object possesses due to its position or configuration. For instance, water stored in a dam at height or a stretched spring has potential energy.
 
• The sum of kinetic and potential energy in a system constitutes its total **mechanical energy.**
 
• This classification of mechanical energy into two types is widely accepted in physics and forms the basis for understanding energy transfer in mechanical systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**

 
 
• Mathematically, kinetic energy is expressed as KE=12mv2" id="MathJax-Element-6-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">KE=12mv2KE=12mv2" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">KE=12mv2KE=12mv2
 KE=12mv2
 KE = \frac{1}{2}mv² , where **m** is the mass of the object and **v** is its velocity.
 
• Kinetic energy is directly proportional to the mass and square of the velocity, meaning an increase in either will increase the kinetic energy.
 
• Examples include moving vehicles, flying airplanes, and running athletes.
 
 
 
• **Potential Energy:**
 
 
• Potential energy is calculated using the formula PE=mgh" id="MathJax-Element-7-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">PE=mghPE=mgh" id="MathJax-Element-2-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">PE=mghPE=mgh
 PE=mgh
 PE = mgh , where **m** is the mass, **g** is the acceleration due to gravity, and **h** is the height.
 
• It depends on the object's position relative to a reference point, such as the height of an object above the ground.
 
• Examples include water stored in a dam, a compressed spring, or a pendulum at its highest point.
 
 
 
• **Energy Conversion:**
 
 
• Mechanical energy can transform between kinetic and potential energy. For example, in a pendulum, energy constantly shifts between these two forms.
 
• In a roller coaster, the mechanical energy is conserved as the cars move up and down the tracks, swapping kinetic energy for potential energy and vice versa.
 
 
 
• **Real-World Applications:**
 
 
• Mechanical energy is utilized in various machines, engines, and systems such as wind turbines, hydropower plants, and mechanical clocks.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in engineering, physics, and various technological applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation of Mechanical Energy:**

 
 
• Mechanical energy is conserved in an isolated system where only conservative forces (like gravity) are acting.
 
• This principle is fundamental to solving many physics problems, such as calculating the motion of a projectile or the dynamics of a pendulum.
 
 
 
• **Non-Conservative Forces:**
 
 
• When non-conservative forces like friction or air resistance act on a system, mechanical energy is not conserved, as some energy is converted into heat or other forms.
 
• This explains why a rolling ball eventually comes to a stop or why energy losses occur in real-world machines.

questions.question: Which of the following sequences correctly represents flow of genetic info?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA → RNA → Protein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The correct sequence of the flow of genetic information is **DNA → RNA → Protein**, commonly referred to as the **Central Dogma of Molecular Biology**.
 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)** acts as the genetic material, storing all the information necessary for the synthesis of proteins.
 
• **RNA (Ribonucleic Acid)** is synthesized from DNA in a process called **transcription**. This RNA (typically mRNA) acts as a template for protein synthesis.
 
• **Protein synthesis**, also known as **translation**, occurs at the ribosome where mRNA is decoded to assemble amino acids into a polypeptide chain.
 
• This process is essential for cellular functions, as proteins serve as enzymes, structural components, and signaling molecules in all living organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Dogma of Molecular Biology**

 
 
• The concept was first proposed by Francis Crick in 1958.
 
• It explains the flow of genetic information within a biological system, stating that DNA is transcribed into RNA, and RNA is translated into protein.
 
• This principle is fundamental to molecular biology and underlies the mechanism of gene expression.

questions.question:
Two resistors, one with a resistance of 2 ohms and the other with a resistance of 4 ohms, are connected in parallel to a 6-volt battery.

What is the total current flowing through the circuit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.5 Amperes**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The two resistors of **2 ohms** and **4 ohms** are connected in **parallel**. In a parallel circuit, the total resistance is calculated using the formula: 
**1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂**. 
• Substituting the values: 
**1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4**. 
Thus, **Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 4/3 ohms**. 
• The circuit is powered by a **6-volt battery**. Using **Ohm’s Law** (**V = IR**), the total current can be calculated: 
**Iₜₒₜₐₗ = V/Rₜₒₜₐₗ**. 
Substitute the values: 
**Iₜₒₜₐₗ = 6 / (4/3) = 6 × 3/4 = 4.5 Amperes**. 
• Hence, the total current flowing through the circuit is **4.5 Amperes**. 
• Each resistor shares the current based on its resistance. The **current through the 2-ohm resistor** is: 
**I = V/R = 6/2 = 3 Amperes**. 
The **current through the 4-ohm resistor** is: 
**I = V/R = 6/4 = 1.5 Amperes**. 
Adding these gives **4.5 Amperes**, verifying the calculation. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Ohm’s Law:** 
• **Ohm’s Law** states that the current flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided the temperature remains constant. 
• The formula is: **V = IR**, where **V** is voltage, **I** is current, and **R** is resistance. 
• **Parallel Circuit Properties:** 
• In a parallel circuit, the **voltage across all components remains the same**. 
• The total resistance in a parallel circuit is always **less than the smallest individual resistance**. 
• The total current is the **sum of the currents through each parallel branch**. 
• **Resistor Applications:** 
• Resistors are widely used in electrical circuits for **current regulation, voltage division, and protection against overcurrent**. 
• They are categorized as **fixed resistors** (constant resistance) or **variable resistors** (adjustable resistance). 
• **Battery Characteristics:** 
• A battery is a device that converts chemical energy into electrical energy. The **voltage rating** of a battery determines the electric potential difference it can provide. 
• Common batteries include **AA, AAA, lithium-ion, and lead-acid batteries**, used in various applications like household electronics, vehicles, and industrial equipment. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Series vs. Parallel Circuits:** 
• **Series Circuit:** The current remains constant throughout the circuit, and the total resistance is the sum of individual resistances (**Rₜₒₜₐₗ = R₁ + R₂ + …**). 
• **Parallel Circuit:** The voltage remains constant across all branches, and the total resistance is calculated using **1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + …**. 
• **Electrical Safety:** 
• To prevent electrical hazards, circuits are often equipped with **fuses, circuit breakers, and insulation materials**. 
• Proper resistance calculations are critical to ensure **safe operation and avoid overheating**. 
• **Practical Examples:** 
• Parallel circuits are commonly found in **home electrical systems**, ensuring that individual appliances function independently. 
• Series circuits are used in applications like **string lights**, where the current flows through all components sequentially.

questions.question:
Read the following and choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): Sound waves travel faster in steel than in air at the same temperature.

Reason (R): The particles in solids (like steel) are more closely packed and experience stronger intermolecular forces compared to particles in gases (like air), allowing vibrations to be transmitted more efficiently and rapidly.

options.text: A is false but R is true..
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sound waves travel faster in steel than in air** because the density and elastic properties of steel allow efficient transmission of vibrations.
 
• Steel, being a solid, has particles that are **closely packed**, enabling faster propagation of sound waves.
 
• In contrast, air, being a gas, has particles that are far apart, leading to slower transmission of sound waves.
 
• **Intermolecular forces in solids** like steel are stronger, which helps in quicker transfer of energy between particles.
 
• The speed of sound in steel is approximately **5,960 m/s**, while in air, it is around **343 m/s** at room temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sound Wave Propagation:**

 
 
• Sound waves are mechanical waves that require a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel.
 
• The speed of sound depends on the medium's density and elasticity.
 
 
 
• **Elastic Modulus and Density:**
 
 
• The elastic modulus (stiffness of the material) is higher in steel, contributing to faster sound propagation.
 
• Density affects sound speed inversely: lower density generally leads to slower sound speed in gases compared to solids.
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Forces:**
 
 
• Stronger intermolecular forces in solids ensure quicker energy transfer between particles.
 
• In gases, weaker forces and larger intermolecular distances result in slower sound transmission.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Sound in Different Media:**
 
 
• Steel: ~5,960 m/s
 
• Water: ~1,480 m/s
 
• Air: ~343 m/s
 
• These values vary with temperature and material composition.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Effects:**
 
 
• In gases, the speed of sound increases with temperature due to increased kinetic energy of particles.
 
• In solids and liquids, temperature changes have a lesser impact compared to gases.

questions.question: Venus is the _______ brightest object in the sky.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Venus** is the **third** brightest natural object in the Earth's sky, ranked only after the **Sun** and the **Moon**.
 
• Its **maximum apparent magnitude** can reach approximately **-4.6 to -4.9**, making it bright enough to be seen during the daytime under ideal atmospheric conditions.
 
• The high visibility of the planet earned it the names **Morning Star** and **Evening Star**, as it appears at its brightest shortly before **sunrise** or shortly after **sunset**.
 
• The primary reason for its extreme brightness is its **Albedo**; **Venus** reflects about **70%** of the sunlight that hits it due to a thick, permanent cover of **sulfuric acid clouds**.
 
• It is the **second planet** from the **Sun**, orbiting at an average distance of about **108 million kilometers** (approximately **0.72 Astronomical Units**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Earth's Twin**:

 
 
• **Venus** is often referred to as **Earth's sister planet** or twin because they are very similar in **size**, **mass**, and **density**.
 
• The diameter of **Venus** is roughly **12,104 kilometers**, which is about **95%** of Earth's diameter.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure and Temperature**:
 
 
• It possesses the **densest atmosphere** of the four terrestrial planets, consisting of over **96% carbon dioxide**.
 
• This leads to a runaway **greenhouse effect**, making it the **hottest planet** in the solar system with surface temperatures averaging **464 degrees Celsius** (**867 degrees Fahrenheit**).
 
• The **surface pressure** is about **92 times** that of Earth, equivalent to the pressure **900 meters** deep in Earth's oceans.
 
 
 
• **Unique Rotation**:
 
 
• **Venus** exhibits **retrograde rotation**, meaning it rotates on its axis from **East to West**, which is opposite to most planets in the solar system.
 
• A single **sidereal day** on **Venus** lasts about **243 Earth days**, which is actually longer than its **orbital period** (year) of **225 Earth days**.
 
 
 
• **Moons and Rings**:
 
 
• Like **Mercury**, **Venus** is unique in our solar system for having **no natural satellites** (moons) and **no planetary rings**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Phases of Venus**: Much like the **Moon**, **Venus** goes through distinct **phases**. This was first observed by **Galileo Galilei** in **1610**, providing critical evidence for the **heliocentric (Sun-centered) model** of the solar system.
 
• **Space Missions**: **Venus** was the first planet to be visited by a spacecraft (**Mariner 2** in **1962**) and the first to be successfully landed upon (**Venera 7** by the **Soviet Union** in **1970**).
 
• **Surface Features**: Radar mapping by **NASA's Magellan** mission in the **1990s** revealed a surface dominated by **volcanic activity**, **mountains** (such as **Maxwell Montes**), and vast **lava plains**.
 
• **Transits**: A **Transit of Venus** occurs when the planet passes directly between the **Earth** and the **Sun**; these are rare events that happen in pairs separated by **eight years**, with intervals of more than a **century** between pairs. The most recent transits occurred in **2004** and **2012**.

questions.question: What is the function of the lysosomes in animal cells?

options.text: Break down waste materials and cellular debris

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Break down waste materials and cellular debris**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound organelles found in **animal cells**. They are often referred to as the "suicide bags" of the cell due to their ability to break down cellular components.
 
• The primary function of lysosomes is to break down **waste materials** and cellular debris. They contain hydrolytic enzymes that are capable of digesting proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids.
 
• Lysosomes play a critical role in **autophagy**, a process where damaged organelles and unnecessary cellular components are digested and recycled to maintain cellular health.
 
• They are also involved in the **immune response** by destroying pathogens and microorganisms that enter the cell through processes like phagocytosis.
 
• Lysosomes contribute to cellular homeostasis by removing potentially harmful substances and preventing the accumulation of toxic materials. *Hence, the correct answer is to break down waste materials and cellular debris.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Lysosomes:**

 
 
• Lysosomes are surrounded by a single phospholipid bilayer membrane and contain a variety of **acid hydrolases** that function optimally at a low pH (around 4.5-5).
 
• The acidic environment is maintained by proton pumps located on the lysosomal membrane.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Lysosomes:**
 
 
• Lysosomes are involved in processes like **autophagy**, where cellular components are recycled to maintain cell health.
 
• They also play a role in **endocytosis** and **phagocytosis**, where they digest substances that enter the cell.
 
• **Example:** Lysosomes in macrophages help break down pathogens during an immune response.
 
 
 
• **Differences in Plant and Animal Cells:**
 
 
• Plant cells generally lack lysosomes, but similar functions are performed by vacuoles.
 
• Animal cells rely on lysosomes for efficient waste management and recycling.

• **Other Functions of Lysosomes:**

 
 
• Lysosomes play a role in **apoptosis**, or programmed cell death, ensuring the removal of damaged or diseased cells.
 
• They are involved in the storage and release of enzymes required for breaking down extracellular materials.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Lysosomal Disorders:**
 
 
• **Tay-Sachs disease:** A genetic disorder caused by lysosomal enzyme deficiency leading to accumulation of harmful substances in neurons.
 
• **Pompe disease:** Caused by a deficiency in the enzyme required for glycogen breakdown within lysosomes.
